title: A search platform turns image-removal control into a trackable request and repeat-protection route
source_unit: Google Search product account of non-consensual explicit-image removal controls
geography: United States; Google Search users and people seeking removal of explicit images

user_control_route.value: people can request removal of non-consensual explicit images from Search and submit multiple images through a simpler form

status_visibility.value: the Results about you hub lets people track request status and receive email notifications when the status changes

repeat_protection.value: users can opt into safeguards intended to filter similar explicit results on an ongoing basis

verified_outcome.value: not observed in the product account
verified_outcome.unit: missing request completion, complete de-indexing, recurrence, survivor safety, wellbeing, trust, and durable exit

observations.method: Extraction from Google's official product account; request submission, status visibility, and ongoing filtering are retained separately from actual removal and later user outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The account is a product announcement and does not report request volume, completion time, removal success, false positives, recurrence, geographic scope of de-indexing, or user-level safety and wellbeing.
observations.subgroup: People seeking removal of non-consensual explicit images from Google Search; no representative user sample or outcome panel is provided.
observations.counterinterpretation: A simpler request form and status notifications can reduce navigation burden while leaving the underlying content, copies on other platforms, and repeated exposure unresolved.

related_sources.claim: The FTC provides a federal escalation route when covered platforms fail to remove qualifying non-consensual intimate images within the statutory period.
People can report platforms that fail to provide a removal process or fail to remove the image and known copies.

boundary: This record adds a user-facing digital-control stage: a simpler removal request, request-status visibility, and an optional repeat-protection feature. It does not establish completed removal, removal across other services, recurrence prevention, survivor safety, wellbeing, trust, or practical exit from the search/platform ecosystem.
